angle: Unlike notation-first network summaries, this video motivates the whole architecture from the 28x28 digit problem via an edges-to-parts-to-digits ladder and a hand-setting-the-weights thought experiment.
angle_detail: Start with [09:08] through [12:27], where weights, the squish function, and the bias threshold turn into the thirteen-thousand-dials count that makes learning necessary. Then read [13:32] through [15:05] for the compact matrix-plus-vector notation the course will use afterward. Note the boundary stated at [16:13]: training itself is deferred to part two, outputs are only counted rather than designed, and the closing guest stretch revises the activation story toward ReLU.
